---
title: Template Selection
description: How to choose a template, where selection happens, and what to expect afterwards.
---

## What is selectable

**All fifteen core templates are selectable.** The registry is closed: an id that is not
on this list is refused rather than silently replaced.

```
row  editorial  canvas  prism  terminal  pulse  brutal  arcade  sketch
signature  saffron  pulsenova  prismnova  terminalnova  arcadenova
```

The **default is `row`**. A configuration that predates template selection, or that
stores an unknown id, resets to `row` and says so.

## Where selection happens

**On a fresh install**, the installer offers the designs directly and asks you to pick
one:

```
Choose your Row-Template design
  1  Row
  2  Editorial
  …
Select [1-15, Enter=Row]:
```

Pressing Enter takes **Row**. Nothing is applied until you confirm the summary.

**After installation**, switch designs from the manager:

```bash
row-template
```

Then choose **2 Reconfigure → 4 Template**. The switch is a full
snapshot/validate/activate transaction, so a failed switch restores the previous design.

> **`row-template config` does not select a template.** That command changes branding
> only — service name, support URL and logo.

## Selecting without a terminal

`RT_TEMPLATE` is read by the **install** path only. It is an environment variable, so the
script it applies to must be reachable — which in practice means you are running the
`install.sh` from an **extracted release bundle**:

```bash
RT_TEMPLATE=prism bash install.sh
```

It also works with the remote one-liner, because the environment is inherited:

```bash
RT_TEMPLATE=prism bash <(curl -fsSL https://github.com/frank0live/Row-Template/releases/latest/download/install.sh)
```

**It has no effect on an existing installation.** `row-template config` does not read it —
use the manager for a post-install switch.

An id that is not on the list is refused, and the error names the available ones:

```
RT_TEMPLATE='xyz' is not a template this release offers (available: row editorial …)
```

**The list is closed on purpose.** A typo cannot silently install a different design.

## What selection actually does

The installer keeps **one verified artifact per design** in a template store under the
install root, each with its own checksum. Selecting a design stages that artifact as the
served page, then reconciles the live page to it.

Because every artifact is verified against its own checksum, a selection cannot end up
half-applied: either the chosen design is live, or the previous state is restored.

## What to expect afterwards

```bash
row-template verify
```

The verification reports the selected design and confirms the served page matches it:

```
Template: Row
Canonical artifact matches the selected template.
```

A configuration that names one design while another is live is the one state the
verification must never report as healthy — so it reports it as a failure.

## Choosing between them

The honest way to compare is structural, not by colour. The
[gallery comparison](/templates/#compare-by-structure) lists every design by layout
family, composition, density, grouping and width.

A useful test: because the designs differ structurally, viewing them in grayscale still
tells them apart. A design that only differs by hue is not a different design.

## What switching does not change

- **Your branding** — service name, support link and logo persist.
- **Your subscribers' data.**
- **The runtime, the locales, or the QR behaviour.**
